entries.summary:
Ich Georg von wellwart ritter ain gemain man zwischen dem edeln hern Fridrichen von Gundelfingen vnd den von Horhain vff ain siten vnd den ersamen geistlichen hern hern
hainrichen dem apt vnd dem Conuent des gotzhus ze Mulbrunn vff die andern siten vergich vnd tun kunt menglichen mit disem brief von solicher stozz zwainung vnd zu sprüch
ansprach [?] so sy ze baider syt zu ainander gehabt hand von Horhain von Gunderbach der dörffer [?] vnd der wald so dar zu gehört vnd Stambach des hoffs wie sich daz bis vff disen hütigen
tag erloffen hant vff mich bekomen sint als vff ain gemain man Vnd do satzt der edel [?] herr Fridrich von Gundelfingen von sinen vnd der von Horhain wegen zu herren Hansen von
Hornstain von Schatzberg [?] ritter vnd Hansen von Lustnow do satzt min herr der apt vnd der Conuent von Mulbrunn vff die andern siten zu mir Cuntzen münch von Rosenberg
vogt ze Stainsperg [?] vnd Raben von Helmstat herrn Rabens saligen sün Vnd do wir fünf also gesessen vnd baider partien clag zu sprüch red vnd widerred verhorten So
haben wir vorgenanten fünf die vorgenanten baid [?] partien mit ir baider wort willen vnd wissen ainmütiglich mit der minn [?] vber ain braucht Also als hernach geschriben stat Des
ersten daz der kouffbrief den min herr der apt vnd der Conuent vorgut [?] hand vmb Gunderbach daz dorff vnd Stambach den hoff by allen sinen kreften beliben sol baider obgenanten
partien mall maß [?] als daz der selb brief vßwiset Ouch sol iegliche party ainen schidlichen man dar geben Vnd da sol denn ieglicher zu jm nemen syben erber manne
den die sachen kundig sint vnd die weder tail noch gemain dar an hand Vnd die zwen vnd mit jn die vierzehen von baiden partyen sullen denn ain kuntschaft erfaren
von der güter wegen die in dem kouffbrief nit begriffen sint dar vmb sy stözzig sint vnd ain vnder gang vollgan lassen Vnd were daz sy ze baider sit nit vber ain komen
mohten so sullen die zwen ainen obman vber sich nemen vnd waz sich da die dry [?] vnd der merer tail mit kuntschaft vnd vndergang dar vmb erkennen da by sol es beliben
Vnd sullen ouch also die vnder gänger liplich ayd zu den hailigen sweren baider partien also vnder ze gan vnd sy ze entscheiden nieman weder ze lieb noch ze laid alles an arglist
vnd an all geuerde Ouch ist me gerett von des hofs wegen ze Stambach daz da sinr [?] nit me da sin sol noch vffbraucht werden denn sehs hertstat vngeuarlich Es ist ouch
mit namen gerett daz solich gult vnd bett die die von Horhain bis her gefordert hand von des hoffs wegen ze Stambach sin [?] ganczlich ab sin sullen vnd sullen sin [?] kain ansprach
noch vordrung me dar nach han in dehain wis vngeuarlich Were aber daz sich vff andern güten die nit in den hoff gehorten dehain gelt bett oder zins mit ainer kuntschaft erfunde
da sol herrn Fridrichen von Gundelfingen vnd den von Horhain ire recht behalten sin Vnd sullen ouch also die kuntschaft laiten vnd all vorgeschriben sach gentzlichen vsstragen vnd
vff die gut komen von morn vber vierzehen tag Vnd welhe party daz nit getun [?] mocht die sol daz der andern vier tag vor widerbieten vnd sol denn dar nach vber ain tag vnd vierzehen
tag vsgetragen werden Vnd möcht daz denn aber nit gesin so sol es aber von dem tag [?] vber ain tag vnd vierzehen vsgetragen werden also daz es in den nehsten dry vierzehen
tagen ain ganczen vsstrag neme vngeuarlich Vnd sullen dar vff ze baider syt gut frund sin vnd sol all vientschaft [?] vnd schad ietweder syt ganczlichen ab sin an all arglist vnd
geuerde vnd aller vorgeschriben ding zu ainer waren vrkund vnd geczugnüß daz es ze baiden siten also ewiglich belibe vnd gehalten werde So han wir die obgenanten Georg von
wellwart der gemain ritter Hanns von Hornstain ritter Hanns von Lustnow Cuntz münch von Rosenberg vnd Raben von Helmstat edelknecht baider partien rantlut [?] vnser ieglicher sin
Insigel an disen brief gehangen Der geben ist vnd diß geschach zu Gruningen [?] des jars do man zalt von gottes geburt tusent drühundert vnd nun vnd nuntzig jare vff
sant Egidien tag des hailigen bychter [?]

entries.english:
I, Georg von Wellwart, Ritter, common arbiter between the noble lord Friedrich von Gundelfingen and those of Horrheim on the one side, and the honourable spiritual lord, Herr Heinrich the abbot, and the convent of the monastery at Maulbronn on the other side, declare and make known to all with this letter: concerning the disputes, dissensions and claims [?] which they have had against each other on both sides concerning Gunderbach, the villages [?] and the forest belonging to it, and Stambach, the Hof, as these have run up to this present day, they have been referred to me as common arbiter. Then the noble [?] lord Friedrich von Gundelfingen appointed, on behalf of himself and those of Horrheim, Herr Hans von Hornstein von Schatzberg [?], Ritter, and Hans von Lustnau; and my lord the abbot and the convent of Maulbronn on the other side appointed to me Kunz Münch von Rosenberg, Vogt zu Stainsperg [?], and Raban von Helmstadt, son of the late Herr Raben. When we five had thus sat and heard the complaint, claim, speech and reply of both parties, we, the aforesaid five, with the knowledge and will of both parties, have unanimously [?] arranged it amicably [?] as written below.

First, that the purchase deed which my lord the abbot and the convent [vorgut?] concerning Gunderbach the village and Stambach the Hof shall remain in all its force, [for] both aforesaid parties [mall maß?], as the same deed states. Each party shall also name an impartial man, and each shall take seven honest men who know the matter and who have no share in it, neither party nor community. The two, and with them the fourteen from both parties, shall then investigate by testimony the properties not covered by the purchase deed, about which they are in dispute, and carry out an inspection (Untergang). If they cannot agree on both sides, the two shall take an umpire over them, and what the three [?] and the majority decide about it by testimony and inspection shall stand. The inspectors shall also swear a bodily oath to the saints to both parties to proceed thus and to decide for no one out of love or hatred, without deceit and without risk.

It was also further agreed concerning the Hof at Stambach that there shall be no more there [?] nor be established than six hearths, approximately. It is also expressly agreed that the dues and levies which those of Horrheim have so far demanded on account of the Hof at Stambach shall be entirely abolished [?], and they shall make no further claim or demand in any way. But if on other properties not belonging to the Hof any money, levy or rent should be found by testimony, Friedrich von Gundelfingen and those of Horrheim shall keep their rights there.

The testimony shall be led and all the above-written matters fully settled, and they shall come to the properties from tomorrow in fourteen days; and the party that cannot do this [?] shall announce it to the other four days before, and it shall then be settled after one day and fourteen days. If that again cannot be, it shall be settled from that day [?] after one day and fourteen, so that within the next three fourteen-day periods a full settlement is reached, without risk. And both sides shall then be good friends, and all enmity [?] and harm on either side shall be entirely abolished, without deceit and risk.

In true testimony and witness of all the above-written things, that they be kept and observed on both sides for ever, we, the aforesaid Georg von Wellwart, common Ritter; Hans von Hornstein, Ritter; Hans von Lustnau; Kunz Münch von Rosenberg; and Raban von Helmstadt, Edelknecht, [rantlut?] of both parties, each of us has hung his seal on this letter. Given and done at Gruningen [?], in the year 1399 after God's birth, on St. Giles's day, the holy confessor [?].
